summaryBox.title: Cryoscopy
summaryBox.takeaway: ΔT_f = T°_f - T_f = K_f · m. Solutions freeze at lower temperatures than pure solvents.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
FREEZING POINT DEPRESSION (ΔT_f)

ΔT_f = T°_f - T_f = K_f × m = K_f × (w_B × 1000) / (M_B × w_A in g)

Thermodynamic Formula for K_f:
K_f = (R × M_A × (T°_f)²) / (1000 × Δ_fus H)
Units of K_f: K·kg/mol (Characteristic of solvent)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Freezing Point Depression**: Adding a non-volatile solute lowers the freezing point of the solvent because the liquid vapor pressure curve intersects the solid vapor pressure curve at a lower temperature: $\mathbf{\Delta T_f = K_f \cdot m}$.
• **Thermodynamic Relation**: $K_f = \frac{R M_A (T_f^\circ)^2}{1000 \Delta_{\text{fus}} H}$.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.2 Antifreeze Chemistry & De-icing Roads
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.2 Antifreeze Chemistry & De-icing Roads
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ANTIFREEZE & DE-ICING APPLICATIONS

1. Automobile Antifreeze: Adding Ethylene Glycol (HO-CH₂CH₂-OH, 35% v/v) depresses water's freezing point to -17.8°C (255.4 K), preventing radiator cracking.
2. De-icing Roads: Spreading NaCl or CaCl₂ on snow depresses freezing point, melting ice at sub-zero temperatures (CaCl₂ produces 3 ions, more effective than NaCl).
conceptBreakdown.content: Ethylene glycol ($35\%\ v/v$) depresses the freezing point of water to $-17.8^\circ\text{C}$ ($255.4\text{ K}$) and elevates the boiling point to $108.9^\circ\text{C}$, providing round-the-year engine protection.

quickRevision: Ethylene glycol is used as automobile radiator antifreeze.
CaCl₂ is more effective than NaCl for de-icing (i=3 vs i=2).
